title: Musa meets al-Khidr
hookLine: Musa travels to learn from a servant given knowledge, and promises patience (18:65–70)
carry: you won't be able to be patient
tomorrow: The boat, the boy, the wall
last: TWO GARDENS — NO POWER BUT HIS.

lines: THE TEACHER GOES LOOKING FOR A TEACHER.
cards: Musa has stood before Pharaoh, crossed the sea, received the Torah. And in a hadith in Bukhari, someone asks him: who is the most knowledgeable person on earth? He says: I am.
God corrects him: there is a servant of Mine, where the two seas meet, who knows more than you. So the great teacher packs a bag and goes looking for a teacher, one who won't let him ask questions.

teach.b: In the hadith, God tells Musa to carry a fish in a basket: where you lose the fish, you'll find him. Musa sets out with a young servant, named Yusha' in the hadith.
At a rock by the sea they rest, and the fish slips into the water and swims off, leaving a strange tunnel in the sea. The young man forgets to mention it.
Later, tired and hungry, Musa asks for their meal, and the young man remembers.

teach.h: THE PLACE WHERE THE SEAS MEET.
teach.b: That's the place, Musa says. They retrace their steps. And there, the Qur'an says, they find one of Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Our presence.

The hadith calls him al-Khidr, the green one, because, it says, where he sat on bare ground, it turned green. Musa asks, very politely: may I follow you, so that you teach me some of the right guidance you've been taught?
The answer, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! thou canst not bear with me." How could you be patient with what you can't fully understand?
Musa replies: in sha' Allah, you will find me patient, and I won't disobey you in anything.
Al-Khidr sets one condition: if you follow me, don't ask me about anything until I bring it up myself.

teach.h: LO! THOU CANST NOT BEAR WITH ME.
teach.b: Musa, a prophet who spoke with God, agrees to be a student who keeps quiet. That's the lesson before any of the lessons. The man who answered I am still had something to learn, and he was willing to walk to find it.

how: Muslim teachers use the story of Musa and al-Khidr to teach the manners of learning: humility before a teacher, patience, and not presuming one knows the most; it is read with all of al-Kahf on Fridays.

o: the brother who spoke for Musa before Pharaoh
the green one, the servant Musa learned from
the young servant who carried the fish

games.q: inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: where you lose it, you'll find him
the green one; named in hadith

s: it calls him one of Our servants; the name comes from hadith.
Musa replies to the warning with in sha' Allah
18:69: you will find me patient, if God wills.
al-Khidr agrees to answer every question as they go
his condition is the opposite: ask nothing until he brings it up.

games.q: you've traveled far to learn from a stranger, and his first words are: you won't be able to be patient with me. what does Musa do?
o: argue that he's a prophet and can manage.
say: if God wills you'll find me patient, and I won't disobey you.
games.why: he promises patience with in sha' Allah, and accepts the condition to ask nothing until he's told.

practice: Bring to mind someone you don't usually learn from: someone younger, or with less schooling, or someone you disagree with, and ask, what do they know that I don't?
Let the answer come slowly: how to fix something, how to be calm, how to live on less. Then imagine asking them about it and, like Musa, keeping quiet long enough to hear the answer.

wordCard.voice: Al-Khidr. The servant of God that Musa traveled to learn from, patient with knowledge Musa was told he couldn't bear. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: al-Khidr, the green one; the name given in hadith to the servant Musa met (also said al-Khidr or al-Khadir).

carryVoice: Your line: you won't be able to be patient. Even Musa had a teacher to find. See you tomorrow.
